text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Government names Thierry Breton new head for Thomson Mutlimedia, setting privatisation process in motion.
-- State considers offering larger stake France Telecom telecommunications operator than originally planned. Hopes to sell 25-35 percent of the capital and to raise 35-45 billion francs.
-- Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Peyrelevade to reshuffle management team.
-- Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer rules out reconsidering decision to shut-down an assembly plant in Belgium despite widespread protest and demonstrations.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Prime Minister's office seeks to privatise Thomson-CSF within six months, terms and conditions to be publicised today.

-- President Jacques Chirac's call for a cut in value-added tax on multimedia products and services would depend on both European Commission's agreement and unanimous agreement by the fifteen EU member countries.
-- COB stock exchange watchdog recommends caution to subscribers of an increase in capital Metaleurop.
L'AGEFI
-- Government to hasten and widen scope of privatisation programme planned for 1997.
-- Survey shows 43 percent of British fund managers see EMU implemented by January 1st 1999.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Real-estate sector expects a pickup in 1997.
-- Advertising agency Euro-RSCG-GBHR wins Cegetel mobile phones advertising budget.
-- Defense Ministry says Aerospatiale may not take part in Alcatel-Alsthom's bid for Thomson-CSF since it is a state-owned firm, following recommendation by privatisation committee.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Up to 9,000 staff from European countries demonstrate at Billancourt site against planned Renault restructuring.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Asset-sale veteran Thierry Breton to run Thomson before privatisation.
